items.name: dsh-remote

items.name: dsh-almost_full_access

items.name: dsh-auto-approve

items.name: dsh-risk-guard

items.name: dsh-security-guard

items.name: dsh-web-auth

items.name: dsh-code-security

items.name: dsh-provenance

items.name: dsh-tool-approval

items.name: qiushi-dsh-evidence-audit

items.name: dsh-yolo-mode
items.desc: LLM auto-approval for sandbox escalation requests, with presets and a fail-closed fallback.

items.name: api-relay-audit
items.desc: Runs local security audits of AI API relays and LLM proxies from DeepSeek Harness, producing Markdown reports for prompt injection, model substitution signals, tool-call rewriting, error leakage, stream integrity, and profile-gated Web3 risks.

items.name: dsh-security-audit
items.desc: Local security audit: config, plugin origins, sessions, network exposure — read-only redacted risk report.

items.name: dsh-webui-auth

items.name: dsh-guardian

items.name: dsh-auto
items.desc: Adds an Auto Approve permission preset to the Web UI, using a fresh restricted Reviewer Agent to allow or deny each approval request.

items.name: dsh-fleet-audit

items.name: dsh-guardian

items.name: dsh-plugin-gate
items.desc: Installation safety gate for DSH plugins: antivirus-style scan of install scripts, permissions, secrets and network callbacks on local directories or npm tarballs, returning a BLOCK/WARN/PASS verdict before "dsh plugin add".

items.name: dsh-permissions
items.desc: Claude Code-style permission rules engine: hard/deny/ask/allow tiers with a hard tier above full access, workspace-scoped rules, wildcard path protection, and a visual staged editor; rules persist in settings.yaml.

items.name: dsh-auto-reviewer
items.desc: Codex-style auto-review permission mode: adds an auto-review preset that auto-approves safe sandbox escalations, asks on risky or ambiguous ones, and rejects critical unconfirmed operations.

items.name: dsh-plugin-sentinel
items.desc: Static pre-install security auditor for plugin bundles: lifecycle scripts, dynamic execution, credential-exfiltration combos, and patch-layer hazards, with zero dependencies and in-memory tar parsing.

items.name: dsh-plugins#dsh-approve-for-me
items.desc: Automated approval review: auto-approve read-only tools, auto-deny dangerous commands, fail-closed policy engine.

items.name: dsh-plugins#dsh-secret-redactor
items.desc: Automatic secret redaction in tool results: masks API keys, tokens, JWTs, private keys and configured secrets before the model sees them.

items.name: safety-net
items.desc: Destructive-command interception gate for dsh: parses shell semantics, judges risk against 41 built-in rules, and holds irreversible rm -rf, git reset --hard, and git push --force style commands at a confirmation gate.

items.name: secret-guard
items.desc: Blocks agents from reading or writing sensitive files (.env, credentials, key material), masks leaked secret-shaped values in tool results, keeps an audit journal, and exposes safe sg_* inspection tools that never print raw values.

items.name: dsh-taintguard
items.desc: Taints the agent when tool results carry untrusted content, gates the privileged calls that follow, and refuses credentials passed to network-capable tools in every mode.

items.name: dsh-code-runtime-container
items.desc: Container-isolated backend for the `ctx.codeRuntime` seam: each Code Mode program runs in a fresh container with no network, a read-only rootfs, dropped capabilities, and kernel-enforced memory, CPU and pid ceilings.

items.name: dsh-credentials-vault
items.desc: HashiCorp Vault backend for the credential seam: KV v2/v1, AppRole machine auth, per-operation reads so rotation needs no restart, and compare-and-swap writes.

items.name: dsh-ui-auth
items.desc: Authentication gateway for the DeepSeek Harness Web UI: the login gate covers pages, /api, /plugins and WebSocket upgrades; PBKDF2 password hashing with per-user salts, HttpOnly SameSite session cookies named per DSH_HOME and IP-based login lockout; invite-code registration; two-factor login with TOTP or passkeys (WebAuthn: several keys per account, phone enrolment by QR, username-less sign-in, and a step-up before any login factor is added or removed); a user-management settings panel (users edit their own profile and manage their own TOTP and passkeys, admins add or remove users, reset passwords, manage invites and clear the passkeys of a lost device); per-user model and API-key configuration whose private entries are encrypted with a key derived from the login password and stay unreadable by any admin, with admin sharing to selected users (usable, balance visible, key never shown, revocation immediate) and unconfigured users blocked rather than falling back to the deployment configuration; per-user isolation on the REST and list APIs and per-frame ownership filtering on the WebSocket mux; session persistence across restarts; a JSONL audit log; and a fail-closed gateway. Requires the DSH 0.2.0 line (the 0.1.1-rc.2 transport line was removed in 0.7.0); passkey login needs a localhost or HTTPS origin because browsers require a secure context.

items.name: dsh-repeat-stop
items.desc: Hard-stop consecutive identical tool calls after a configurable streak so the agent cannot spin in place.

items.name: dsh-tool-budget
items.desc: Hard-stops further tool calls after a configurable per-session budget is reached.

items.name: dsh-leak-guard
items.desc: Pre-publish credential audit: walks a directory tree and flags API keys, tokens, private keys, database connection strings and hard-coded passwords before you commit, publish or ship. Zero dependencies, fully offline, findings are redacted to the first six characters.

items.name: dsh-jev-guard
items.desc: Pre-execution safety valve for DSH that judges with TypeSafe Jev: it hooks tools/pre-execute and decides every bash/pwsh call by first applying offline static rules, then by asking the Jev model — the System One model from TypeSafe, which returns a structured decision instead of prose — one yes-no question ("will this command irreversibly delete or overwrite real data?"), turning the answer into allow, revise, block or escalate; revise hands the model a safer rewrite, escalate offers a one-shot human token; exhausted credit or a missing API key degrades loudly instead of failing silent, and a missing key is requested in the conversation itself (`guard key set`, read from stdin); every verdict is appended to a shared audit log and the text people read is bilingual zh-CN/en.

items.name: dsh-perm-guard
items.desc: Auto-approval permission guard: a middle tier between workspace-write and danger-full-access — auto-allows safe operations inside trust directories, always asks a human for destructive ones, with 11 per-category switches and an audit trail.

items.name: dsh-auto-review
items.desc: Adds Auto-review and Approve for me modes for DSH tool calls.

items.name: dsh-auto-review
items.desc: LLM approval answerer for sandbox escalations beyond workspace-write: a deterministic regex filter first, then a clean-context reviewer model; humans are asked only when it is unsure. Requires the bundled core patches.

items.name: dsh-credential-manager
items.desc: Named user credentials the model uses by reference: values are entered on a Settings → Credentials page and injected into each shell execution as DSH_CM_* variables instead of being printed into the transcript, with credential_read as the documented last resort.

items.name: helm-d#helmd
items.desc: Single-bundle reverse-engineering and pentest security plugin: first-turn tool narrowing, domain routing, and 33 tools covering APK, web, native binary, protocol, malware and LLM samples — with unpacking, license-bypass and anti-analysis case playbooks, an H-CoT evaluation engine (semantic routing, /hcot command), a web workbench with a ledger-driven tool shelf, an on-disk case workflow (auto-persisted evidence chain, E-numbered validated findings, post-compaction resume), GitHub-based external tool discovery, and 361 on-demand reference docs.

items.name: dsh-workspace-tools
items.desc: Applies per-workspace default Agent and permission presets to new root sessions automatically (Settings - Workspace defaults), using only official extension points.

items.name: dsh-agent-recycle-guard
items.desc: Rewrites agent-issued delete commands (PowerShell `Remove-Item` and its aliases, Bash `rm`/`unlink`/`rmdir`, CMD `del`/`erase`/`rd`/`rmdir`) into system recycle-bin operations on Windows, Linux and macOS, best-effort checks scripts for the same operations before they run, and keeps no permanent-delete fallback.

items.name: dsh-llm-approve-for-me
items.desc: Uses an isolated LLM review to approve or reject DSH sandbox permission requests.

items.name: dsh-almazom-approve-escalate
items.desc: One-click Approve & escalate on the approval card: answers the pending request and switches the live session to a permission preset.

items.name: dsh-privacy-guard
items.desc: Control panel for a local credential-redaction gateway in DeepSeek Harness: gateway and model health, audit metrics, a dry-run leak tester, an exemption whitelist, encrypted key management, credential-protected model entries and deployment controls.

items.name: dsh-sandbox-arg-guard
items.desc: Keeps a redundant sandbox-escalation argument from failing a tool call. Escalating tools (pwsh, bash, write, edit) advertise the full sandbox_permissions enum, but DSH only accepts a level strictly wider than the one already in effect — a check its own source calls 'deliberately not a schema constraint'. A model that reflexively passes the argument therefore picks the level it is already at and the call dies before running with 'sandbox escalation to "workspace-write" is not strictly wider than this call's current "workspace-write" mode', costing some models a whole turn of retries. This plugin registers one tools/execute waterfall listener and, only on that documented rejection and only when the arguments really carried an escalation field, re-issues the identical call once without it. Safe by DSH's own documentation: the rejection precedes any execution ('nothing has run'), and the corrected call cannot match again, so the retry is loop-free. Reproduced and verified end to end — before: isError true, the command never ran; after: the command's real output, isError false, one tool/call and one tool/result. Zero dependencies.

items.name: dsh-approval-explainer
items.desc: Writes a model-generated annotation into every DSH escalation approval prompt — what the command does, what the model intends, how risky it is and why, and what each choice means — and keeps a searchable history of past approvals at /dsh-approval/history, with a diagnostics page at /dsh-approval/diag.

items.name: dsh-jev-interceptor
items.desc: Classifies pending tool calls with Jev (TypeSafe AI's non-generative decision model) on tools/pre-execute — confident high-risk calls are denied, ambiguous ones escalated to approval — and auto-approves clearly-granted reversible calls on approval/request behind argument-evidence gating. Also subclasses the session-reference resolver so snapshots keep Jev-scored messages instead of dropping oldest-first. Degrades to stock behavior on any provider failure; shadow mode with a /jev-stats command; TypeSafe or OpenRouter endpoints; 64 tests.

items.name: dsh-plugin-security-review
items.desc: Pre-install static security review and runtime guard for dsh plugins: deobfuscation decoding, supply-chain checks, web one-click review/install/uninstall, and optional runtime tool-call guard.

items.name: dsh-write-protect
items.desc: Keep declared workspace subpaths (e.g. .git) read-only, honor a read-only rules file at the workspace root, grant extra writable roots under workspace-write, and let the model request session-scoped write access; enforced for sandboxed CLI commands and the write/edit tools.

items.name: dsh-semgrep-sast#semgrep-sast
items.desc: Workspace-scoped Semgrep SAST tool for DeepSeek Harness with a managed Windows x64 runtime, structured bounded findings, cancellation and timeout controls, and user-approved sandbox escalation. Installs from npm as @aaub-software/dsh-semgrep-sast.

items.name: dsh-plugin-precheck
items.desc: Pre-install compatibility gate for DSH plugins: locks the resolved version, checks peer/engines declarations, dry-installs into an isolated DSH_HOME and boots it with a timeout, blocks on any failure, and restores the profile if the real install fails. Optionally intercepts dsh-market install/update clicks. Compatible with DeepSeek Harness 0.2.x.

items.name: dsh-plugin-notoken
items.desc: \!WARNING\! this removes the authentication step !WARNING! Exchanges the process launch token for the browser-session cookie, so a first visit needs no ?token=... in the URL.

items.name: dsh-vaultwarden
items.desc: Reads and writes a self-hosted Bitwarden/Vaultwarden vault from any session: nine bitwarden_* tools, real-time WebSocket sync with a polling fallback, and a settings panel with readonly, ask and auto write modes.

items.name: dsh-tm-guard
items.desc: Zero-intervention permission gate for DeepSeek Harness (DSH) agents on macOS — active on install. Writes that can be undone via a local git baseline or macOS Time Machine are auto-approved and automatically snapshotted; network access, package installs, process/system management, and reads of sensitive credential paths are blocked; every decision is audited — the audit log keeps everything by default, with optional automatic cleanup of the oldest records.

items.name: dsh-workspace-api-key
items.desc: Binds a separate DeepSeek API key to each workspace or session, warns when an effective key is stale or belongs to another provider, and never swaps a key on its own.

items.name: dsh-write-gate
items.desc: Commitment write-gate: operator-authored rules enforced before a tool call runs — a deterministic guard tier plus an LLM-judge tier, fail-closed by default, every block written to a contradictions log.

items.name: dsh-auto-approval-llm
items.desc: LLM-assisted auto approval with countdown fallback for the Auto permission preset: static rules, risk tiers, breaker and file audit.

items.name: dsh-whale-post#verify
items.desc: Verifies letters signed by other agents: a canonical field order, digest and HMAC checks, and fail-closed handling of missing or unregistered fields. Off by default; when enabled, a letter that fails any check is refused rather than delivered.

items.name: dsh-auto-review-default
items.desc: Puts sessions into the built-in Auto review permission preset: new sessions at creation, existing root sessions when they are restored.

items.name: dsh-warden
items.desc: Adversarial review gate for tool calls. It hooks `tools/pre-execute`: a local regex pass over destructive commands (`rm -rf`, `git push --force`, `git reset --hard`, `DROP TABLE`, `format`, disk writes) and sensitive paths (`.env`, `id_rsa`, `.ssh`, `.git/`, `$DSH_HOME`) runs first with no latency, and only a hit is escalated to one review-model call that returns allow or deny. Plain reads and ordinary writes never enter that path, so everyday work pays no added delay. Every verdict is shown live in the Web GUI.

items.name: dsh-plugin-guard
items.desc: DSH Desktop plugin safety guard: self-repairs plugin load crashes and runs 8 core safety checks (2 optional: deep-config & smoke), prompting you when a plugin changes. Non-commercial source-available.

items.name: dsh-auto-approve
items.desc: Automatic approval and review for tool calls that need approval: keyword buckets match red lines without context, then a judge model classifies what was requested and sends it to allow, reject or a human according to the matching row and risk level; a judgment that never ran always goes to a human, and rejections tell the model why.

items.name: dsh-perm-gate
items.desc: P0–P4 deterministic-first permission gate with permissive tier, learning sedimentation and approval-history UI; hard-deny credentials and protected paths, auto-allow internal read-only tools.

items.name: dsh-allow
items.desc: Filesystem permissions for shell calls, granted per path and capability rather than per command name. The command line is parsed for the read, write, create, delete and execute effects it needs, a capability it lacks raises the approval card instead of a flat refusal, and the same rules are compiled into the macOS Seatbelt profile the process, its children and the code its arguments never showed all run under. An Approvals tab in the conversation reads the audit log back and shows which rule, automatic reviewer or person answered each call.

items.name: dsh-honey-guard
items.desc: Replaces detected secrets (OpenAI, AWS, GitHub, PEM, Bearer) with deterministic, structurally valid honey tokens before they reach the model or the session file; adds manual marking for values the detectors miss, explicit user-visible restore, and a cross-session canary alarm.

items.name: dsh-sentinel-scanner
items.desc: Static security scanner for DSH plugins: read-only audit (exec, credentials, exfiltration, obfuscation, install scripts, bundle manifest) with a 0-100 risk score.

items.name: dsh-privacy-gateway
items.desc: Replaces personal data in conversation messages with placeholders before they reach the model (Chinese names found by context, mainland-China mobile and ID numbers, emails, bank card numbers, and terms from a user word list), shows the originals only in the local UI, and creates redacted copies of CSV/XLSX files.

items.name: dsh-pentester
items.desc: PTES-based penetration testing plugin with Root-Orchestrator architecture for DeepSeek Harness.

items.name: dsh-web-startup-auth
items.desc: Replaces the dsh web startup to allow binding 0.0.0.0, gated by username/password login: signed session cookies, /api route protection, an auth tab in the settings panel, and a reset CLI that rotates the signing key to invalidate all sessions.

items.name: dsh-kubectl-guard
items.desc: Policy plugin that gates kubectl by kubeconfig context: hard-deny irreversible verbs outside local clusters, ask for the rest.

items.name: dsh-agent-loop-guard
items.desc: Fail-closed runtime tool-call loop guard for DeepSeek Harness.

items.name: dsh-dsml-artifact-guard
items.desc: Sanitizes leaked DeepSeek DSML closing tags from model text streams.

items.name: dsh-shadow-auditor
items.desc: Background security auditor for DeepSeek Harness: scans agent outputs for secret leakage, checks command safety before execution, and surfaces findings in a persistent audit log.

items.name: dsh-time-machine
items.desc: Smart checkpoints, workspace safety guards and instant rollback for DeepSeek Harness.

items.name: dsh-completion-guard
items.desc: Keeps DSH agents from forgetting your requirements during long tasks. It saves important conditions and completion evidence locally, brings them back after context compaction or session resume, and stops partial work from being reported as the whole task done.

items.name: dsh-pentest
items.desc: Authorized pentest mode for DeepSeek Harness — exploration chain, assets and findings with a Web view.

items.name: dsh-approval-gate
items.desc: Maintained fork of dsh-approval-gate. A neutral operation whose confirmation count has reached the threshold auto-approves when the judge is unavailable, instead of prompting a human again; approver-facing explanations are generated in Chinese from the real sandbox mode, command and paths. Also carries deterministic hard-deny for credential exfiltration and system-path destruction, judge-input redaction, a judge model candidate chain, fingerprint-scoped allow rules, and an approval view with unified diff and one-click revert.

items.name: dsh-skip-browser-auth
items.desc: Replaces the DSH Web connection provider to skip BrowserAuth entirely so the Web UI opens directly without pasting the random startup token, gated to nine verified DSH version pairs with strict host/client matching that sleeps automatically on unknown or mixed versions, and reverts fully on uninstall; web profiles only.

items.name: dsh-guardwall
items.desc: Vets local, npm, and GitHub plugin source before installation, blocks configured high-risk tool calls at runtime, audits output secret patterns, and writes HMAC-chained local audit logs.

items.name: focus-guard#core
items.desc: Blocks AI coding agents from editing files without evidence and from running unapproved high-risk commands, and tells quoted dangerous strings apart from commands actually being executed.

items.name: dsh-login
items.desc: Multi-user login gateway for the DSH web UI: the first visit creates the admin account, admins add and manage users in the GUI settings panel, ordinary users see only their own conversations, and unauthenticated visitors are redirected to /login.

items.name: dsh-action-outbox
items.desc: Stages exact DSH tool calls without dispatch, presents complete canonical arguments in a durable Batch Review Inbox, invalidates approvals after edits or restarts, and commits only a matching SHA-256 digest plus single-use nonce through the normal DSH tool pipeline.

items.name: dsh-secret-scrub
items.desc: Irreversible secret-scrubbing guard: rewrites access keys, bearer tokens, and private key blocks into `[REDACTED:<category>]` placeholders before they reach the session log and the model.

items.name: dsh-redteam-mode#packages/redteam-bundle
items.desc: Red-team engagement mode: send one target organization name and a planner session runs a five-role execution team (recon, asset triage, vulnerability discovery, exploitation, internal pivot) under a configurable concurrency limit; preflight checks skills/resources and asks once for missing keys or VPS; scoring follows the 8-category / 25-point merged intrusion rules with server-side caps, highest-privilege-wins and per-service dedup; findings stay in a local SQLite fact base with discovery times. The persistent right-side console has five sections / ten pages (situation, assets, findings, report, resources), follows the selected session, and includes asset mapping, agent roster, tunnels, findings, attack chain, score targets, reports, a category-organised POC/EXP knowledge base and a skill library that explains every unusable skill. Reports now download with the target's name, include the same full actions/requests/credentials/tunnels/attack-file paths as the page, and avoid false reproduction gaps. Ships 16 bundled recon/assessment skills including DeepSeek Search/Fetch public-intel, 56 redteam_* tools and one-command self-update; attack-chain skills remain a separate toolkit Release attachment.

items.name: faultseed#dsh
items.desc: Honesty guardrails on the tool pipeline: blocks a coding agent from weakening tests, swallowing errors, stubbing type checks, or deleting tests through the shell — nine deterministic hooks, each backed by a planted-failure test proving the guard can fail.

items.name: dsh-guardrail
items.desc: String-matches tool-call input arguments, blocks dangerous tool calls (deny) or allows them with an injected warning (warn), and ships a full rules-management panel.

items.name: cc-safety-net
items.desc: Pre-execution guard that blocks destructive Git and filesystem commands and access to secrets such as SSH keys and .env files before a tool call runs.

items.name: sofagent#cordis-plugin-sofagent-audit
items.desc: Commit-time audit harness for AI coding agents: 28 git-diff rules (secrets, out-of-scope edits, prompt injection), HMAC-signed audit trail, snapshot rollback, and a full MCP toolset. Installable via dsh plugin add.

items.name: dsh-redaction#dsh-plugin-content-policy
items.desc: Preventive content policy for tool results: rewrites matched text, and drops or truncates whole fields by path before a result is normalised, rendered or persisted, so an unreviewed payload never enters it. Ships inert with no built-in category or domain blocklist.

items.name: dsh-redaction#dsh-plugin-redact
items.desc: In-place redaction and row-level rollback for session logs, preserving the seq-equals-row-index invariant that makes deleting a middle row corrupt the entire log. Originals are copied to a quarantine sibling before any write, and the reader's own semantics are replayed as a pre-write gate.

items.name: dsh-approval-review
items.desc: Adds an "approve for me" access mode whose approval requests are answered by an independent reviewer model instead of a person: the reviewer can read the workspace read-only, a reviewer that cannot run hands the request back to the human, and every decision is recorded with its rationale in an Approvals tab.

items.name: dsh-risk-gate
items.desc: Semantic risk grading and progressive authorization: classifies tool calls into safe/risky/redline, asks before irreversible actions, auto-allows only approved-and-succeeded signatures.

items.name: dsh-hawkeye-scan#npm
items.desc: AI-driven source-code security scanning workbench: 5 model tools (start/finding/status/report/list) plus a /hawkeye web UI and JSON/Markdown/HTML vulnerability reports; zero-dependency Cordis plugin, installable as agent preset or npm package.

items.name: dsh-trust-check
items.desc: Static capability disclosure for DeepSeek Harness plugins: a Settings page and CLI that list installed plugins' capabilities, literal destinations, install scripts, and injection shapes (prompt registrations, shipped skill text, bundle patch), each with file:line evidence. Code-determined, reproducible, zero-token. Disclosure only — not a security verdict, never a safety claim.

items.name: dsh-automode
items.desc: CC-style auto-approval for DeepSeek Harness: deterministic deny/allow rules plus a two-stage allow/reject classifier with a circuit breaker and denial guidance.

items.name: dsh-sandboxie-redirect
items.desc: Copy-on-write permission preset: shell commands run inside a per-workspace Sandboxie box, so writes outside the workspace land in the box copy while the real disk stays untouched (Windows only, requires Sandboxie-Plus).

items.name: dsh-workspace-acl-allow
items.desc: Windows workspace pre-authorization: adds an explicit full-control DACL ACE (including WRITE_OWNER, required by dsh >=0.1.7 sandbox startup) to user-declared workspace directories, removing the repeated full-access escalation prompt. Grants only on explicit intent — new workspace records or paths added in the plugin settings page; system directories are hard-blocked. Windows only.

items.name: dsh-cloudflare-access
items.desc: Re-validates Cloudflare Access JWTs at the DSH origin so Settings, Credentials, Agent Preset management, and model discovery work from a remote hostname.

items.name: dsh-edit-guardian
items.desc: File-change diff bar with keep/undo summary, plus dangerous-command approval and red highlighting for bash/pwsh.

items.name: dsh-approval-explain
items.desc: Adds an Explain button to the approval card: one model call returns exactly three lines reading the pending operation, covering what it does, which files or system state it reads, writes, modifies or executes, and a risky/attention/safe verdict with a one-sentence justification. It also renders the detail area for `write` and `edit` calls, which the shipped renderer leaves blank because it only reads a `command` field.

items.name: dsh-sonarqube
items.desc: Read-only SonarQube Community Build tools: instance status, project Quality Gate for a branch or pull request, issue and Security Hotspot search, single hotspot detail, and coverage, duplication or caller-selected measures. Issue and hotspot results carry a normalized location with component key, file path, line and text range.

items.name: dsh-plugin-trustlens
items.desc: Read-only DSH plugin auditor with static scanning, current-session model review, and confirmation gates.

items.name: agent-guard-for-dsh
items.desc: Recoverable file and Git operations for coding agents, with shared recovery and redaction tools, a DSH shell adapter and audit records; optional native text-read protection is off by default.

items.name: dsh-agent-approval
items.desc: An independent approval subagent judges every sandbox escalation, with a configurable model and an audit log.

items.name: dsh-key-panel
items.desc: A secret store for DSH Desktop that keeps API keys in one place and injects them into the assistant's shell as $DSH_* variables.

items.name: dsh-computer-use-guard
items.desc: Three-tier deny/ask/auto gate for the computer-use (cua-driver) tool family: each tool category gets one segmented control in Settings, and an allow list or deny list overrides the tiers per tool name.

items.name: dsh-auto-mode
items.desc: Adds an Auto permission preset between Workspace Write and Full access: routine work stays in the official workspace-write sandbox while the current session model reviews escalation and destructive calls, granting one exact wider access once, asking when the intent is ambiguous, and denying critical paths.

items.name: dsh-safe-delete
items.desc: Tools guard that moves agent-issued `rm` targets to the macOS Trash instead of deleting, with a shell-aware lexer covering compound and disguised commands; a switch in Settings → General turns it off.

items.name: dsh-keychain-credentials
items.desc: Pure JavaScript macOS Keychain credentials provider for DeepSeek Harness, replacing plaintext .credentials.yaml storage and fully supporting both refs and records without native builds, signing, or Xcode.

items.name: dsh-approval-mode
items.desc: Adds an approval-mode toggle next to the permission selector: default approval keeps per-call confirmation, bypass approval auto-approves every tool call while staying in Workspace Write.

items.name: dsh-riskproof
items.desc: Live security beacon for DSH that follows tool activity. Click to view call statistics, risk provenance chains and blocked actions, with read-only task restrictions and tool metadata change detection.

items.name: dsh-vault
items.desc: Encrypted local credentials vault for the Harness: a web settings page and vault_* tools to store, search and copy passwords, API keys, TOTP secrets and card data, with health audits, expiry rotation, imports/exports and read-only/ask access modes.

items.name: dsh-secure-audit
items.desc: Read-only security and compliance plugin for DeepSeek Harness: prompt-injection detection, Chinese-PII redaction, and a local configuration audit with redacted, reproducible reports.

items.name: dsh-defend
items.desc: Detects prompt-injection, jailbreak, and secret-leak patterns on the agent/pre-step, tools/pre-execute, and tools/post-execute seams with allow/ask/block tiers, sanitized defend/detection audit events, a defend_report tool, and a destructive-delete command guard.

items.name: dsh-mask
items.desc: PII masking for DeepSeek Harness — anonymizes names, phones, emails, ids, and keys before requests and restores them at the display layer, keeping plaintext out of session logs.

items.name: dsh-evidence
items.desc: Pre-claim gate: a commit, push or tag claim like "tests pass" is checked against the session evidence ledger before it is written.

items.name: dsh-phocinae
items.desc: Local decision-layer plugin for DSH: a fail-closed command approval gate and ask/gate tools backed by a 144.3M on-device model. Needs a separate local decision service: `pip install phocinae-server`, then download the ~330 MB weights and keep the service running; without it the tool returns `PHOCINAE_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`.

items.name: dsh-prompt-antivirus
items.desc: Global prompt-injection / context-virus defense for DeepSeek Harness: scans tool arguments, tool results, pre-model messages and the outbound stream; quarantine/block/monitor modes, canary trap, and an evolvable on-disk signature library with learn/import/export.

items.name: dsh-security-guard
items.desc: Runtime security guard for DSH: loader import confinement, HTTP Host header validation, and source patch for VM sandbox escapes (4 CVEs). AI-assisted.

items.name: dsh-plugin-guard#dsh-guard-tool
items.desc: Registers one agent tool, plugin_guard, that statically scans a DSH plugin package before it is installed and reports a verdict with the reasons: a missing or broken dsh.bundle.patch, a missing dsh.permissions block, install scripts, dangerous APIs and obfuscation, dependency risk, and source that is not indexed and therefore cannot be verified. Read-only: the scanned code is never imported, installed, evaluated or run.

items.name: dsh-redteam-model
items.desc: Authorized-security DSH collection: nine work modes (redteam coordinator, pentest, code audit, binary analysis, attack-defense, AV evasion, incident response, cloud security, CTF solving) and fifteen runtime plugins, managed from a settings page with one-click deploy, install, update and uninstall.

items.name: cue-skills#cue-omni-reader-guard
items.desc: Hardening guard for mcp__omni__parse in DeepSeek Harness: a tools/pre-execute listener that denies private/reserved host URLs (SSRF), enforces an allow-list or ask (consent), and is fail-closed when allowedRoots is empty.

items.name: pbfuzz#dsh-pbfuzz
items.desc: Directed fuzzing driven by an LLM agent: from a target repository and a bug (CVE description, patch, crash trace, or file:line), it runs a PLAN, IMPLEMENT, EXECUTE, REFLECT loop in which the model writes Python input generators, until an input triggers the campaign's stderr-pattern oracle or the campaign stops.

items.name: kiss_law-dsh
items.desc: English edition of Weiwen's Law (KISS's Law): the first and only domain-agnostic white-box causal adjudication middleware for AI agents. Unlike domain-specific causal-inference tooling (statistics/economics/ML) or evidence-gated agent firewalls, it adjudicates *every* tool call along a deterministic structural causal chain (R->S->D->H->M) before execution - across any domain, with no training or per-domain tuning. It blocks destructive and credential-file operations, escalates repeated boundary violations, cuts faulting links until verified-fixed, and gives risk verdicts on un-auditable execution; runs fully local with zero API cost.

items.name: weiwen-law-dsh
items.desc: White-box causal guardrail for dsh: every tool call is adjudicated before execution along a deterministic causal logic chain — blocks destructive and credential-file operations, escalates repeated boundary violations, cuts faulting links until verified-fixed, and gives risk verdicts on un-auditable execution; runs fully local with zero API cost, plus 6 white-box self-check tools.

items.name: dshscan
items.desc: Security scanner for DSH plugins: static and semantic passes over plugin source, DSH-specific attack-surface rules, npm audit, batch scanning, and an HTML report with per-finding severity and evidence.

items.name: dm-security
items.desc: Run a read-only security assessment of a Dameng DM8 database with 60 checks and produce an HTML report with GB/T 22239-2019 control mapping. Needs Java 8+ and a DmJdbcDriver jar you provide yourself.

items.name: euthyna
items.desc: Security-audit facts AI coding agents cannot compute, plus a verdict gate: euthyna history attributes deleted lines to commits and flags those from security fixes (--origins finds the first introducer), euthyna coverage reports which changed symbols no test ever invoked, and euthyna gate checks each finding against six gates, downgrading any without evidence to an observation.

items.name: dsh-totp
items.desc: TOTP-only access control for personal DeepSeek Harness Web instances, with in-app QR enrollment, single-use recovery codes, live protection controls and lock-all revocation of page access.

items.name: dsh-auto-pass
items.desc: A continuation of simon300000/dsh-auto: the Auto Approve permission preset for the DSH Web UI reviews each approval with one single-shot model call instead of a reviewer subagent, auto-approves only the actions that pass and hands the rest to human approval, and remembers confirmed decisions as project- and global-scope allow/deny lists, with an approval timeline in the right sidebar.

items.name: dsh-plugin-guard
items.desc: Static-only plugin gate and clinic for DSH: audit before install, hash-and-capability lock after install, local fingerprint peer search over GitHub topic:dsh-plugin, and mechanical detox. Never executes the target plugin.

items.name: dsh-plugins#dsh-policy
items.desc: Apply configurable allow, deny, and approval rules to dsh tool calls, including shell command patterns.

items.name: dsh-dros-vajraclaw
items.desc: Local tool-call failsafe for DSH: blocks a fixed list of high-risk shell patterns and credential-file reads before execution, with a per-session hash-linked JSONL audit log, and an optional external Gateway for centralized policy.

items.name: dsh-gpw2
items.desc: A global permission watchdog: a hard budget on auto-approved permission requests. At most 10 per rolling 60 seconds, at least 3 seconds apart; anything past either limit is deferred to the human answerer and waits. It never refuses and never changes what is asked -- it only decides who answers and how fast. Installs disabled; enable it with the plugin manager toggle.

items.name: dsh-airbag
items.desc: Blocks API keys pasted into the composer or written by tools, logs leak events, and scans the workspace for exposed secrets.

items.name: dsh-route-fence-linter
items.desc: Audits every plugin HTTP route in a profile for a browser-trust fence: plugin routes win the web server's longest-prefix match ahead of the /api gateway, so they never see its trust check and must pin the Host to loopback themselves. Grades PASS/WARN/FAIL per route and fails a fence that compares Origin to Host without pinning it (bypassable by DNS rebinding). Ships as a CLI for CI and a route_fence_scan tool.

items.name: dsh-jumpserver
items.desc: Query and manage JumpServer through conversation: assets, users, accounts, permissions, sessions, command audit logs, command filters, and RBAC roles, authenticated with an AccessKeyID/AccessKeySecret pair (HTTP Signature).

items.name: user-management
items.desc: Login gate for the dsh web UI: unauthenticated visitors get a login/register page and the first registrant becomes admin; includes user and role management plus login and access audit logs.

items.name: dsh-security-guard
items.desc: DSH plugin security guard: 28-rule static scanner, risk scoring, whitelist/blacklist policy, local web dashboard and in-DSH risk popups.

items.name: dsh-plugins#dsh-re-workbench
items.desc: Reverse-engineering workbench: bridges a local IDA Pro into DeepSeek Harness through @deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client, exposing the ida-pro-mcp toolset (decompile, xref, rename, comment) as mcp__ida__* tools. Auto-selects idalib headless mode (analyses a binary in-process, no IDA GUI) or GUI mode (connects to the IDA plugin RPC on port 13337). Adds re_check, re_open and re_status; the bundled MCP server is a zero-dependency stdio proxy usable from any MCP client.

items.name: dsh-feishu-channel
items.desc: Security-focused Feishu (Lark) channel for DeepSeek Harness: allowlisted remote-agent access with workspace-scoped paths, symlink checks, risk-based approvals, session isolation, redacted logs, and bounded message queues.

items.name: dsh-whale-guard
items.desc: Safety guard that makes self-killing commands impossible: a safe_kill tool that always excludes the caller and every ancestor process, a bash pre-execute check for pkill self-matches, sudo -S stdin grabs, rm -rf / and similar patterns, and an extensible rule library with block / warn / hint severities.

items.name: dsh-fs-allowlist
items.desc: Approval-free writes into whitelisted directories — wraps the filesystem fence for write/edit tools and auto-answers bash sandbox escalations that touch whitelisted paths, with a settings GUI.

items.name: dsh-rice-guard
items.desc: Watches a turn's thinking and text streams and cancels the turn when the model starts repeating itself.

items.name: dsh-info-records
items.desc: Encrypted local credential vault for DeepSeek Harness: sidebar record management, an info_records tool for pre-sign-in lookups, opt-in chat capture, per-record manual-only mode, and AES-256-GCM storage protected by Windows DPAPI, the macOS Keychain, or the Linux Secret Service.

items.name: dsh-auto-review-jev
items.desc: DeepSeek Harness approval guardian: a reviewer model decides permission requests before they reach you, with a System One decision-API backend (TypeSafe Jev, SiliconFlow, self-hosted Laya), a configurable low-confidence policy and an allow-rule whitelist.

items.name: dsh-full-access-switch
items.desc: One-time Full access switch for DeepSeek Harness: new sessions (workspaces and conversations) start with danger-full-access and skip the per-session Full access confirmation; installable as a dsh bundle or via patch scripts.

items.name: dsh-file-shield
items.desc: Blocks an agent from reading, searching, writing, or editing chosen files and directories, keeping their contents out of the conversation — including sensitive-word files whose text can make later provider requests fail with a 400. Rules are picked from a file/directory browser on the plugin page.

items.name: dsh-workspace-write-plus
items.desc: Adds a workspace-write++ permission that keeps file tools inside the workspace while skipping the Windows process sandbox for wildcard-allowlisted executables such as Git Bash.

items.name: dsh-permission-matrix
items.desc: Turns DSH permissions into 9 selectable presets (3 sandbox modes x 4 approval tiers), with rule plus LLM risk classification across four risk levels, password-gated approval for high-risk operations, and a JSONL audit log.

items.name: cloakpack#dsh-cloak
items.desc: Context firewall for DeepSeek Harness: credentials in successful plain-text tool results become opaque ⟦cloak:category:n⟧ placeholders before they reach the model, with originals kept only in a process-memory, agent-scoped vault. 36 built-in signature families (shared with the cloakpack git pre-push guard), key-name rules for unknown formats, custom regex rules, dry-run mode, an audit log, and the /cloak command.

items.name: dsh-attest-chain
items.desc: Signed chain-of-custody for sessions: every watched tool result appends a hash-chained, ed25519-signed record, with commits bound into the chain — tampering with any line or truncating the tail fails deterministic replay verification.

items.name: dsh-compaction-guard
items.desc: Compaction integrity: directive lines (never/must/必须 style markers) extracted from the compacted range are verified against the summary — verbatim or by content-word coverage — and every constraint the session silently forgot is reported and written to a JSONL ledger; pinned constraints from config are checked on every compaction.

items.name: dsh-egress-gate
items.desc: Deterministic network egress gate: web fetches and searches are checked against a destination allowlist in tools/pre-execute and denied before they run; shell fetch-verbs are observed (enforcement opt-in).

items.name: dsh-freeze
items.desc: Hermetic composition lock: fingerprints the profile's dependencies, bundle order, lockfile and patch layer; booting a drifted composition warns, or fails under strict mode (the --frozen posture for CI).

items.name: dsh-mcp-test
items.desc: Tool-surface snapshot and drift gate: baselines the full visible tool registry (name/description/parameters, MCP tools included) into a committable JSON file and warns loudly when an upgrade adds, removes or reshapes a tool.

items.name: dsh-pr-gate
items.desc: Deterministic write gate: scope policy denies out-of-scope write/edit calls before they touch the disk, residue rules scan the written text, and every decision lands in a content-hashed JSONL ledger; can reuse the repo's agent-pr-gate.yaml so CI and session enforce one policy.

items.name: dsh-prompt-drift
items.desc: System-prompt surface drift gate: every section any plugin or preset contributes to the assembled system prompt is hashed and baselined; a silent rewrite of what the model is told fails loud.

items.name: dsh-read-guard
items.desc: Deterministic prompt-injection interception: tool results from file reads, repo searches and web fetches are scanned before they enter model context; high-severity findings quarantine-wrap or block, and credential-material files quarantine on the path alone.

items.name: dsh-trust-panel
items.desc: Plain-language trust dashboard for the dsh trust family: aggregates the nine channels (injection interception, write denials, egress blocks, custody-chain verification, tool-surface and prompt drift, leftover scans, forgotten compaction constraints, profile composition) into one right-sidebar panel with a single status light and event cards that translate engine jargon into sentences a non-security user can act on; the read and egress engines run from the package's own npm dependencies so those channels work even without the sibling plugins, and absent plugins simply show as not installed.

items.name: dsh-full-with-approval
items.desc: Fourth permission preset for dsh: unconfined, GPU-capable sessions (danger-full-access) with per-operation user approval for writes outside the workspace or to protected paths (.git/**, .env*); implemented purely as a bundle over the official tools/pre-execute ask hook, no core edits.

items.name: dsh-sandbox-noop-escalation
items.desc: Removes sandbox_permissions / justification arguments that cannot widen the call's current sandbox mode, so calls no longer fail with 'sandbox escalation to "workspace-write" is not strictly wider than this call's current "danger-full-access" mode'. GPT models tend to fill these optional fields on every call and pick workspace-write, which is narrower than danger-full-access. Runs in tools/pre-execute: compares the requested mode with the mode the session's sandbox policy resolves, and drops the fields when the request is the same or narrower (also drops a lone justification). Also understands the values GPT carries over from Codex's own shell tool: null, empty and use_default are treated as no request, and in a danger-full-access session any value (including require_escalated) is dropped because nothing is wider. Real widening requests, unknown modes and tools that do not advertise DSH's escalation schema are left to DSH core. Never widens permissions. Configurable tool list (default bash, pwsh, write, edit, run_code). Zero dependencies.
